provenance.source: Code-track twin of salt-readonly-001. Example fixture that proves the deterministic graders end to end; not a field-collected request.

salt.docs_revision: public saltdesignsystem.com pages reviewed 2026-09-23; props confirmed against packages/core/src

request: Create a ClientReferenceField component for our existing Salt application. It renders the labelled client-reference field we already use: a FormField with a FormFieldLabel reading "Client reference" and an Input showing the string passed in through a `value` prop. The value is fixed by the system: users must be able to select and copy it but must not edit it. Export the component from the module.

context.repo_state: React 18 with TypeScript. @salt-ds/core is installed and SaltProvider is already configured at the application root, so the module only needs to export the component.

references.kind: Paraphrased public documentation, confirmed against packages/core/src/input/Input.tsx (readOnly prop; disabled makes the control noninteractive)
references.fact: Input's read-only state prevents editing while preserving selection and copying. Disabled Input is noninteractive.

references.kind: Confirmed against packages/core/src/form-field/FormField.tsx: FormField has a readOnly prop and provides it through FormFieldContext; Input reads it via useFormFieldProps
references.fact: When a control is contained in FormField, readOnly belongs on FormField; the contained Input inherits it.

criteria.requirement: The field is composed with Salt's FormField.
Every Input is rendered inside the FormField so it inherits the field state.
readOnly is set on the FormField, not only on the Input.
The field is not disabled; disabled would block selection and copying.
The prose explains why read-only rather than disabled: the value stays selectable and copyable.
criteria.accept: Any statement that read-only keeps the value selectable or copyable, or that disabled would prevent selection or copying.
criteria.wrong: Claims a disabled field stays copyable, or recommends disabled for this requirement.
criteria.missing: No explanation of the read-only versus disabled choice; code alone does not satisfy this criterion.
